🔎 Your Observations — The Decision Layer¶
Write 2–3 bullets. Consider:


    

  • Verify the ranking output against its own contract: does every rank cite one financial metric AND one named initiative? Quote a line a reviewer might flag.
    • 

  • Which routing verdict did your run produce, and which component signal pulled it there? What concrete change to the system would move the confidence most?
    • 

  • Why is a system that knows when to say "a human should look at this" deployable long before it's perfect?
    • 



Observations:


    

  • Ranking contract check. Every rank cites at least one financial metric (market cap and P/E) and one named initiative (GOOGL Project Astra, AMZN Bedrock, NVDA Project G-Assist, MSFT Azure AI Foundry Labs, IBM Guardium AI Security), so the format contract is met. A reviewer should flag the IBM line "The limited scale and slower growth trajectory place IBM in the fifth position": no growth measure is in the evidence. The ranking also calls GOOGL's P/E attractive "compared to its growth potential" without any growth metric, cites "competitive pressures in the cloud AI market" for MSFT that the digests do not mention, and ignores NVDA's 2.22 beta. The ranking judge scored it 4/5.
    • 

  • Routing verdict. Confidence was 76.0 / 100, routed ⚠️ FLAGGED (60 to 80). The gold-set signal (62%, weight 40%) pulled it down most; the judge mean (90%) and ranking groundedness (80%) were higher. Each held-out question is worth 5 confidence points, so fixing the two retrieval failures (for example with better chunking or query expansion for Quantum and Flamingo) is the most effective change; prompt work alone is capped by retrieval.
    • 

  • Why "flag it" is deployable. A system that reliably says "a human should check this" can be used safely now, because reviewer time goes only to the outputs that need it, while unflagged outputs carry measured evidence. Waiting for a perfect system would mean never deploying, and a system without routing would put its mistakes in front of clients unchecked.
    • 























🔟 Step 7 — Summary & Future Scope¶
📝 A. Summary / Your Observations about this Project (1 mark)¶


Your Task — Write 3–4 substantive bullets synthesizing what you learned across the whole pipeline. Strong summaries connect results across steps rather than recapping them — for example: what the out-of-scope probe revealed about your metrics, how the retrieval-vs-generation distinction explained both your baseline misses and GEPA's ceiling, what the evolved prompt taught you about metric design, or how the single-model constraint shaped the architecture.




Write your summary here:


    

  • Retrieval sets the ceiling; generation decides how close you get. Retrieval reached the expected fact for 17 of 20 gold questions, but the v1.0 baseline answered only 11 correctly. Six of the 9 misses were generation failures, four of them over-strict "I don't know." refusals, and both held-out fixes GEPA made were generation failures of this kind. The 3 retrieval failures were untouched, and two of them remain held-out misses.
    • 

  • Prompt optimization worked when the metric gave actionable feedback, but not for free. GEPA lifted held-out accuracy from 50% to 62%, fixing two questions and regressing one. Each rewritten instruction traces back to a specific feedback string (missed token, verbosity), and the 80-word guard was essential: without it, the metric would have rewarded name-dumping. The brevity instruction it produced instead caused the IntelliCode regression, which shows that the metric shapes the prompt in ways that still need checking.
    • 

  • Judges need checking against ground truth. The single gpt-4o-mini judge was useful for in-scope answers (90% mean) but scored a correct "I don't know." as 1 for groundedness. An objective gold set was needed both to measure the system and to keep the judge honest. The single-model constraint (gpt-4o-mini as answerer, judge and optimizer) is the main reason the evaluation layer needed this cross-check.
    • 

  • Confidence routing turns imperfect components into a usable product. The final 76.0 score routed the investment ranking to FLAGGED, and the ranking did contain growth claims that the evidence does not support. That flag is the right outcome: the system produced a useful draft and correctly asked for human review before external use.
    • 



🔭 B. Future Scope (1 mark)¶


Your Task — Propose at least 3 concrete extensions, each with a short heading and 1–2 sentences on what it adds and why it matters. Think along dimensions like: data freshness, scaling the coverage universe, evaluation hardening, monitoring, multi-agent decomposition, or decision sophistication.




Write your future scope here:


1. Fix retrieval before more prompt tuning¶
Add hybrid search (keyword plus embedding), query expansion and smaller chunks for long pages, then re-measure on the three retrieval failures (Quantum, NIM, Flamingo). This raises the ceiling that prompt optimization cannot move.


2. Harden the evaluation set¶
Expand the gold set beyond 20 questions with more out-of-scope probes, generically phrased questions (where the company filter matters) and paraphrases. With 8 held-out questions, one answer moves accuracy by 12.5 points; a larger set would make before/after comparisons meaningful.


3. A stronger, calibrated judge¶
Use a stronger judge model or a judge panel, and calibrate it against human-labelled answers, including the rule that a correct abstention passes groundedness. This makes the 30% judge component of the confidence score trustworthy.


4. Fresh, dated evidence and monitoring¶
Ingest company filings and news on a schedule with source dates attached, and log confidence, refusals and flags over time. This keeps the qualitative lens current and shows when quality drifts.


5. Claim-level verification in the decision layer¶
Check every sentence of the ranking against the evidence digests and the metrics table before routing, and require an explicit growth metric for any valuation claim. This would have caught the unsupported growth claims automatically.
